title: Predictive-warmup-autoscaler-with-tenant-budgeted-warm-lanes-and-safe-rollbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a predictive warmup autoscaling policy that provides per-tenant budgeted warm lanes to absorb short bursts while enforcing safe rollback and eviction behavior. The goal is to reduce tail latency regressions during sudden traffic ramps without over-provisioning committed capacity. This ticket covers policy definition, controller implementation, simulation, and integration with rollout/rollback hooks in the Dedicated control plane.
background: Current autoscalers either react too slowly to short-lived bursts (causing p95/p99 latency spikes) or overprovision to avoid spikes, increasing cost for Dedicated customers. We need a middle ground: a small, controlled warm pool that can be temporarily used by tenants using a budgeted credit mechanism and a predictive short-horizon demand estimator to pre-warm lanes. The policy must include safety limits and automatic rollback triggers to avoid sustained overuse or QoS degradation.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Controller exposes a new autoscaling policy type 'predictive-warmup' that can be attached to tenant capacity configs. 2) Each tenant has a configurable warm credit bucket with refill rate and max cap. 3) Short-horizon predictor (EWMA-based) generates warm lane pre-warm events with >85% hit rate on synthetic ramp tests. 4) System enforces safety limits: min_replicas, max_scale_step, cooldown windows, and rollback triggers. 5) End-to-end integration tests and load sims show reduced p95 by >=15% on 30s spikes without increasing steady-state cost by >5%.
design_decisions: - Predictor: EWMA short-horizon (+ optional AR(1) mode for noisy tenants). Chosen for low compute and robustness. - Warm lanes: fixed-size ephemeral slot allocation per tenant drawn from a shared warm pool; allocation consumes tenant credits. - Credits: token-bucket with configurable refill and max cap; used to prevent repeated warm usage by noisy tenants. - Scaling algorithm: dual-loop: fast reactive PD loop for immediate requests and a slow predictive loop that signals pre-warm operations. - Safety: max_scale_step = 2x per 30s, cooldown_base = 60s, min_replicas enforced via tenant contract. - Rollback: automatic rollback to previous model if error_rate increases 3x or p95 latency increases >20% sustained for 2 minutes after warm event. - Observability: emit events for warm allocations, credit consumption, rollback triggers, and predictive confidence scores.
implementation_plan: 1) Add policy schema to autoscaler DSL (API + validation). 2) Implement EWMA predictor service with pluggable config. 3) Implement warm-pool allocator with tenant credit bookkeeping (in Redis-backed store). 4) Extend scale executor to support pre-warm actions (spin up warm lanes on a different GPU class if configured). 5) Wire rollback and safety checks into rollout orchestrator. 6) Build integration tests and chaos tests. 7) Run simulations and a canary against a dedicated test fleet, then gated gradual rollout.
metrics_and_slo_targets: - Primary target metrics: p95 latency (ms), tokens/sec headroom, tail error rate. - Predictor performance: hit_rate on ramp events >= 0.85, false_warm_rate <= 0.10. - Safety thresholds: sustained p95 increase >20% for >120s triggers rollback; error rate spike x3 triggers rollback. - Cost impact: steady-state cost delta <= +5% for tenants using warm lanes. - Resource guards: warm pool usage percent must remain < 25% of total dedicated spare capacity.
safety_limits: - min_replicas: tenant_contract.min_replicas (enforced). - max_scale_step: 2x per 30s window. - cooldown_window: 60s base + 10s per scale_step. - warm_credit_refill: tenant-configurable, default 100 tokens/min, max_cap 500 tokens. - warm_slot_duration: default 90s ephemeral; can be extended with approval. - eviction_grace_period: 30s before forced eviction of warm lanes. - rollback_conditions: p95_increase_pct > 20% sustained 120s OR error_rate_multiplier >= 3 OR GPU_completion_time_increase > 30%.
risks: - Predictor misses large outliers leading to under-provisioning; mitigated by reactive PD loop. - Credit starvation for spiky tenants causing throttled user experience; mitigation: allow opt-in higher credit tiers under contract. - Warm pool exhaustion causing unfairness; mitigation: proportional allocation and tenant QoS tiers. - Complexity in debugging cascading rollbacks; mitigation: structured events and trace links in console.
test_plan: - Unit tests for predictor math and credit logic. - Closed-loop sims with synthetic tenant patterns (sinusoidal, spikes, noise) comparing baseline autoscaler vs predictive-warmup. - Chaos test: simulate delayed warm provisioning and GPU slowdowns. - Canary: roll out to non-production dedicated cluster 1 for 2 weeks with observability dashboard and automated rollback. - Load tests: 30s/60s spike suites verifying p95 improvement and cost impact.
